$comment: Teams Store and Microsoft 365 Copilot validation rules for the three.ws 3D Studio app package, each tied to Microsoft's published guideline and to the check that proves it. check.type: preflight (scripts/lib/microsoft-store-validation.mjs, run by npm run check:microsoft-store), test (a vitest case), browser (a Playwright case), manual (evidence in the reviewer pack). tests/microsoft-store-rules.test.js fails if any rule loses its check.

rules.rule: The package passes Microsoft's own validator (Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit CLI, manifest schema and rule checks).
manifest.json validates against the published v1.30 schema.
The app name does not contain Teams, Microsoft or another Microsoft product name.
The app name does not contain Beta, Dev, Preview, Test or similar prerelease words.
The manifest short name matches the listing name in intro.md and the name the bot uses for itself.
The short description is 80 characters or fewer.
The short description does not use the word app and does not repeat the app name.
The full description is at most 4000 characters and 500 words.
No MS or MSFT abbreviation, no Office 365 (use Microsoft 365), no 'certified for' or 'powered by', no AppSource links, no superlatives.
The first reference to Teams in each description is 'Microsoft Teams'.
The listing states the app's limitations (asynchronous generation time, rate limits).
The full description says the app works with Microsoft 365 Copilot and gives at least one sample prompt.
App, command, parameter and tool descriptions contain no instructional phrases (ignore, new instructions, if the user says, do not print, answer in bold, reset).
Those descriptions contain no URLs, emoji or hidden characters.
Those descriptions contain no superlative claims (#1, amazing, best).
Every MCP tool declares readOnlyHint, and tools that create or change data declare false.
The MCP server and every endpoint answer over HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or later, without redirects, on a domain in validDomains.
Tab pages allow framing by every Teams, Outlook, Microsoft 365, Copilot and Bing host in Microsoft's frame-ancestors list.
Tabs use TeamsJS 2.22 or later.
color.png is a 192x192 PNG on a solid or fully transparent background.
outline.png is a 32x32 PNG, white on a transparent background.
developer.name matches the Partner Center publisher display name exactly.

rules.section: Privacy policy, terms of use and support links
rules.rule: Every URL in the manifest and intro.md answers 200 over HTTPS, with no redirect and no sign-in.

rules.section: Privacy policy, terms of use and support links
rules.rule: The privacy and terms links in the listing are the same links as in the manifest.
validDomains has no wildcards on top-level domains, no schemes or paths, and no Microsoft domains.
Every origin a tab loads inside Teams (content, configuration and in-frame navigation) is in validDomains.
Tabs respond within 2 seconds (median over three loads).
Bot command lists cover exactly the scopes the bot is installed in.
Bot commands have no slash prefix.
The bot lists a help command.
The bot sends one welcome message when installed, naming the app as the manifest does; in a team or chat it says who added it.

check.by: tests/teams-bot-conversation.test.js > welcomes a person once when they add the bot in personal scope

rules.rule: In a team or group chat the welcome mentions who added the bot.

check.by: tests/teams-bot-conversation.test.js > says who added the bot to a team or group chat

rules.rule: The bot answers hi, hello and help.
Help describes every capability and does not send the user outside Teams.

check.by: tests/teams-bot-conversation.test.js > answers help with every capability and no link that leaves Teams

rules.rule: An unknown command gets a valid reply that says what works.

check.by: tests/teams-bot-conversation.test.js > tells the person an unknown command was not recognised

rules.rule: Adaptive Cards the app posts carry at most six actions.

check.by: tests/microsoft-store-rules.test.js > keeps every card the bot posts to six actions or fewer

rules.rule: The meeting stage and side panel use the dark theme whatever the Teams client theme is.

check.by: tests/microsoft-teams-theme.test.js > forces the dark theme on the meeting stage and side panel

rules.rule: A meeting surface that offers sign-in also offers sign-out.

check.by: tests/e2e/microsoft-teams-store.spec.js > side panel offers sign-in when signed out and sign-out when signed in

rules.rule: Each tab renders inside an iframe without a Teams host and logs no console errors.

check.by: tests/e2e/microsoft-teams-store.spec.js > renders in an iframe without TeamsJS

rules.rule: Tabs are responsive at phone width with no horizontal scroll.

check.by: tests/e2e/microsoft-teams-store.spec.js > fits a phone screen with no horizontal scroll

rules.rule: Tabs follow the default, dark and high-contrast Teams themes.

check.by: tests/e2e/microsoft-teams-store.spec.js > follows the default, dark and high-contrast themes

rules.rule: Links that leave Teams carry exit text and a pop-out icon.

check.by: tests/e2e/microsoft-teams-store.spec.js > marks every link that leaves Teams with a pop-out icon

rules.rule: A tab that shows content made by other users gives a way to report it.

check.by: tests/e2e/microsoft-teams-store.spec.js > lets a person report an agent

rules.rule: Surfaces shown on Teams mobile carry no pricing or purchase links.

check.by: tests/e2e/microsoft-teams-store.spec.js > shows no pricing on phone width

rules.rule: Submission carries test notes for every capability and a demo account where sign-in is needed.
The app shows no advertising.
Apps with cryptocurrency features show legal compliance; the Teams app has none, which the questionnaire states.
Copilot tool calls answer at p50 2s, p75 5s, p99 9s; long generation returns a job id at once and is polled.
